why: Insert every number of arr1 as a digit string into a trie; then walk each number of arr2 down the trie, and the depth reached is its longest common prefix with anything in arr1. The maximum depth over arr2 is the answer.
hints: Comparing every pair is 50000 * 50000, too slow. Treat the numbers as digit strings.
Shared prefixes are exactly what a trie stores: insert all of arr1's digit strings, one trie level per digit.
For each number in arr2, follow its digits from the root until a digit has no child; the steps taken are its best prefix length. O(10 * (n + m)) time. (A set of all prefixes of arr1 works too.)
pitfalls: Only cross-array pairs count; don't compare numbers within the same array.
Compare decimal digit strings, not numeric values (544 is a prefix of 5444444).
If no pair shares a first digit the answer is 0.
